title: Le Cygne: Bokor (1925) and Weilerstein (2009)
work: Le Cygne, from Le Carnaval des animaux
question: What happens to the cello’s long song when marimba replaces piano?
intro: At the White House on 4 November 2009, Alisa Weilerstein played Le Cygne with sixteen-year-old Jason Yoder at the marimba. Judith Bokor’s earlier Columbia disc has a pianist accompanying the cello. In both arrangements Saint-Saëns’s long melody is played over broken chords.

recordings.label: Judith Bokor
recordings.note: A Columbia recording for cello and piano, issued on D 9758.

recordings.label: Alisa Weilerstein · Jason Yoder
recordings.note: Live at the White House, with sixteen-year-old Jason Yoder’s marimba accompanying the cello.

passages.label: Opening cello phrase
passages.note: The cello begins its long tune above a stream of broken chords.

passages.label: Rising phrases over broken chords
passages.note: The cello plays rising phrases above the piano’s continuous broken chords.

passages.label: Rising and falling phrases
passages.note: The cello’s phrases rise and fall back, while the piano keeps up its running figuration beneath them.

passages.label: Approach to the high note
passages.note: The cello climbs towards a long high note; beneath it, the piano’s arpeggios continue.

passages.label: Final held note
passages.note: The cello holds a long note above the last piano chords, then stops.
